items.name: SidecarBinary::detect, runtime_dir, search_path
items.what_it_does: Finds the llama.cpp server program on this computer: first an environment variable, then the project's runtime folder, then the system PATH. If none is found, it tells the user to run a build script.
items.change: The pool manager finds the runtime on each GPU machine it controls (one machine) or uses it from the container image (Kubernetes). The runtime version is something the admin chooses, and the error message should speak to the admin, not to an end user.
items.evidence: COMPANION_LLAMA_SERVER_BIN env override; runtime_dir(install_root) = install_root/runtime/bin; search_path over PATH; message 'Run scripts\\build-runtime.ps1 from the project folder'

items.name: SidecarBinary::devices, supports_argument, builtin_chat_templates, help_text, listed_builtin_chat_templates
items.what_it_does: Runs the model server program briefly to ask which GPUs it can use and which options and built-in chat formats it knows. It remembers the help text in memory for each program file.
items.change: Each GPU machine runs this once and reports the result to the pool manager's registry: which devices it has, the runtime build, and which options and chat formats it supports. The in-memory cache is fine to keep as a local speed-up on each machine.

items.name: server_args
items.what_it_does: Builds the start-up options for the model server. It always listens on the machine's own loopback address only and serves one conversation at a time. It also sets context size, GPU layers, cache precision, batch sizes, drafting, threads, the RAM prompt cache and the vision add-on file.
items.change:
Changes needed:
- The listen address becomes configurable: all addresses inside a Kubernetes pod, loopback on one machine.
- The number of parallel conversation slots for each copy becomes an admin setting, and the context per slot is accounted for.
- Each copy can be pinned to a GPU (a device option or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES).
- The builder must be able to produce a vLLM equivalent.
The option-building logic itself stays.
items.evidence: "--host".into(), "127.0.0.1".into(), ... "--parallel".into(), "1".into(); only device option emitted is ["--device","none"] for CPU

items.name: Load-failure explanations: RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTIC_MARKER, without_runtime_diagnostic, last_runtime_error, explain_load_failure, describe_exit
items.what_it_does: Turns the model server's log and exit code into a plain sentence explaining why a model would not start or why it stopped.
items.change: Keep as is. The pool manager stores the sentence on the copy's record so the admin dashboard can show it. Users only see that the model is unavailable.
items.evidence: explain_load_failure matches 'wrong number of tensors', 'key not found in model', 'unknown model architecture'; describe_exit names Windows codes like 0xC0000005

items.name: RunningSidecar::spawn, stop, is_alive, stop_report
items.what_it_does: Starts one model server as a child process on a fixed local port and waits up to 5 minutes for it to report healthy. It keeps the last 8 KB of its output and the process handle in memory, and can stop it or report how it ended.
items.evidence: TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)); base_url = format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"); child: Child stored in struct; crate::logfile::model_server() single model-server log

items.name: reap_orphaned_sidecars, normalized_executable_path
items.what_it_does: Before starting a model, it kills every model-server process on the machine that runs the same program file and whose parent process no longer exists.
items.change: Only reclaim processes the pool manager itself recorded (by process id or a marker file per copy). Otherwise, when several copies run on one machine and the manager restarts (on Windows), starting one copy kills all the others.
items.evidence: process.exe() == target && process.parent().map_or(true, |parent| system.process(parent).is_none()) => process.kill(); called from spawn at line 413

items.name: drain_worker_log, wait_for_health
items.what_it_does: Reads the model server's output into a short in-memory tail and the model-server log on disk. It checks /health every half second until the server is ready or has exited.
items.change: Keep for the local-process backend, with one log per copy. In Kubernetes, the readiness check and pod logs replace both.
items.evidence: bytes.drain(..excess) keeps 8192 bytes; client.get(format!("{base_url}/health")) loop with child.try_wait()

items.name: shared_client
items.what_it_does: Keeps one shared pool of HTTP connections for every model request. It waits 5 seconds to connect and 20 minutes between received bytes.
items.change: Keep it in the gateway client used by API servers and workers. Allow more idle connections per host, because many copies and providers will be called. Outside providers need their own timeouts and their own key header.

items.name: SidecarClient generic OpenAI-format core: ChatTurn, turn_json, native_calls_in, StreamedToolCalls, SseFrames, post_chat, send_with_retry, complete_detailed_body, stream/stream_body, classify_failure/classify_status/transport_failure, StreamHandlers, StreamOutcome, AgentCompletion, NativeToolCall
items.what_it_does: Talks to the model in the standard OpenAI chat format. It sends messages and tool definitions, reads either a whole reply or a streamed one (text, hidden reasoning and tool calls), stops early when a complete action has arrived, and sorts failures into kinds the caller can recover from.
items.change:
Changes needed:
- Make this the OpenAI-format adapter of the model gateway: a base address and API key for each provider, plus a list of which extra fields that provider accepts.
- Add an Anthropic adapter beside it with the same request and response shapes.
- Keep the early-stop and cancel behaviour.
- The OpenAI-compatible endpoint for other company software can reuse the parsing code.
items.evidence: post to format!("{}/v1/chat/completions", self.base_url); delta parsing of /delta/content, /delta/reasoning_content, /delta/tool_calls; [DONE] handling

items.name: llama.cpp-specific client parts: sampling_body, apply_options, structured json_object schema, timings_per_token, template_caps, visible_token_count, tokenize
items.change: Put these behind the llama.cpp adapter, switched on only when a copy runs llama.cpp. A vLLM adapter maps them to vLLM's names (prefix caching is automatic there, sampling names differ, it has its own tokenizer endpoint). Outside providers get only standard fields, and their structured output uses the json_schema format. Token counting falls back to the provider's usage numbers.

items.name: template_safe_turns, flattened_tool_turn, is_template_refusal, strictly_shaped_body
items.what_it_does: Reshapes the message list for models whose chat template refuses a system message or requires strict user/assistant alternation. If the server refuses the list, it retries once with the strictest shape.
items.change: Keep it for self-hosted models (llama.cpp and vLLM both render the model's own template). Read the template's limits from the model's ability profile, not from the current load settings. Outside providers skip it.
items.evidence: template_safe_turns(turns, cfg.chat_template); retry when code == BAD_REQUEST && is_template_refusal(&text)

items.name: observe_prompt_size, prompt_chars, call_chars (with agent::CHARS_PER_TOKEN_X100)
items.what_it_does: After each request, learns how many characters make one token for 'the' model and stores the ratio in one number for the whole program. Every new model load resets it.
items.change: Keep the ratio for each model id. An in-memory cache per process is acceptable because it is only an estimate, but it should be seeded from a stored value so a fresh worker does not start at the default.
items.evidence: crate::agent::observe_prompt(chars, prompt_tokens); agent.rs:117 static CHARS_PER_TOKEN_X100: AtomicU32; api.rs:2059 crate::agent::reset_chars_per_token()

items.name: RecordedRequest, RequestRecorder, without_image_data, record_request, recorded_output
items.what_it_does: Hands a copy of every model request and its reply, with image data removed, to a recorder the caller provides, which saves it.
items.change: Keep it. The recorder becomes the audit and request-log sink, carrying the user, the model id, the copy or provider, and the retention rules.
items.evidence: pub type RequestRecorder = Arc<dyn Fn(RecordedRequest) + Send + Sync>

items.name: structured_action_schema
items.what_it_does: For models that cannot call tools natively, builds a strict answer format listing each built-in tool and its required inputs, so the model can only produce a valid action.
items.change: Build the list from the tools this user and model are actually offered, including plugin and MCP tools from their description files. Emit the format each adapter accepts: llama.cpp's shape or the standard json_schema.
items.evidence: for tool in crate::tools::registry() { let required = crate::tools::required_args(tool.name); ...}; serde_json::json!({"type": "json_object", "schema": {"anyOf": alternatives}})

items.name: Request entry points: chat, chat_turns, agent_chat_turns, probe_turns, agent_chat_turns_stream, chat_turns_without_reasoning, chat_turns_on_run_prompt, chat_stream, chat_turns_stream(_observed)
items.what_it_does: Ready-made request types: a plain chat, an agent step, a short tool-check probe, a check that turns thinking off, and a check that reuses the agent run's own prompt so the cache still matches. Each one takes all its sampling values from the load settings of the running model.
items.change: Take sampling values for each request (resolved from the company, group and user settings) instead of from the load settings. Address requests by model id and conversation id through the gateway, not by a base address.

items.name: LlamaServerManager
items.what_it_does: Holds the single running model server, if any, and the last load error, for the whole application.
items.change: Replace it with the pool manager's registry of copies, stored in PostgreSQL: model id, node, address, state (starting, ready, draining, stopped, failed), slots, runtime build, last error. API servers and workers read this registry or ask the gateway. Only the pool manager holds process handles.

items.name: InferenceStatus
items.what_it_does: Status report naming one engine, one model, one address and one context size.
items.change: Users get an availability list for each model they may use (ready, waking up, unavailable). The admin dashboard gets the status of each copy.

items.name: InferenceError, SidecarFailure
items.what_it_does: Error types for model requests, with plain messages. Some messages tell the user to press Load or change Settings.
items.change: Keep the kinds of failure. Reword the user messages: users can no longer load models or change load settings. Add kinds for 'model has no ready copy', 'provider refused' and 'not allowed'.

items.name: Support, TemplateCaps, ChatTemplateShape
items.what_it_does: Records what a model's chat template can do: tools, system message, alternation. It is read from llama.cpp's /props at load.
items.change: Make these fields part of the stored ability profile for each model. vLLM and outside providers fill them from their own metadata or from probe results.

items.name: InferenceConfig
items.what_it_does: One settings bundle that mixes four things: how to start the model (file path, context, GPU layers, threads, cache), how to sample each reply (temperature and similar), what the model can do (template shape and tool-check result), and its default file 'models/model.gguf'.
items.evidence: pub model_path: PathBuf ... pub tooling: Option<ToolingProfile> ... pub temperature: f32; model_path: PathBuf::from("models/model.gguf")

items.name: speculative_for, DRAFT_HEAD_* constants, default_* helpers
items.what_it_does: Decides how the model server should guess ahead to speed up replies (draft head or n-gram), from the model file's facts and an on/off setting.
items.change: Keep it. The on/off switch becomes an admin performance setting for each deployment.

items.name: EngineTimings
items.what_it_does: Reads llama.cpp's own speed numbers for one reply: prompt speed, generation speed, prompt tokens reused from cache, drafted tokens.
items.change: Keep it inside the llama.cpp adapter. The vLLM and provider adapters leave it empty or fill it from usage data. Cache hits per copy feed the routing-affinity metrics.

items.name: ResolvedRuntimePolicy, resolve_runtime_policy*, VramState, fit_to_memory, cpu_context_cap, prompt_cache_ram_mib, apply_to
items.what_it_does: Plans how one model will fit this machine. It uses the GPU memory free now (counting everything else as used) and the free RAM to choose context size, cache precision and GPU/hybrid/CPU placement. It also sizes the RAM prompt cache and writes explanatory notes. The tuning comes from the single settings object.
items.change: Keep the method. The budget becomes the free memory of the GPU this copy is assigned to, minus memory reserved for copies that are starting. Tuning comes from the admin's settings for the deployment. When a copy has several slots, the context is multiplied by the slot count. Notes go to the admin, not the user.
items.evidence: let free = vram.total_bytes.saturating_sub(vram.used_bytes); note text 'Closing other GPU-heavy applications before loading allows a larger context'; tuning: &crate::settings::RuntimeSettings

items.name: Metrics, OutputTiming
items.what_it_does: Speed and token counts for one reply or one agent turn, kept separate from the reply text.
items.change: Keep. Add the model id and the copy or provider so usage can be shown per user and per model.
items.evidence: pub struct Metrics { tokens_per_sec, prompt_tokens, kv_cache_limit, timing, engine, finish_reason }

items.name: IInferenceEngine, StubEngine, LlamaCppEngine
items.what_it_does: An engine interface that the real code path does not use. A fake 'stub' engine is kept loaded only as a mirror for the status screens, and a placeholder llama.cpp engine always fails.
items.change: Remove all three. The model gateway built from the client code is the real abstraction. Status comes from the pool registry.

items.name: ModelMetadata, ModelCapabilities, validate, gguf_path, deletion_path, safe_gguf_filename
items.what_it_does: Describes one model (name, architecture, size, context, vision, tool support, memory figures) and where its file is in the local models folder. It includes a 'loaded' flag and checks that file names and ids are safe.
items.change: Make it the registry record in PostgreSQL. The location becomes an object-store key or shared-volume path plus a content hash. Remove the 'loaded' flag, because state belongs to each copy. Keep the safety checks for admin imports.

items.what_it_does: Reads only the header of each model file in the local models folder: architecture, context, chat template, memory figures, packaging problems. It also infers names and quantization from file names, finds a vision add-on file next to the weights, and caches headers in memory.
items.change:
Run the header reading once, when the admin imports a model, as a job on a machine that can read the model store. Store the results in the registry. Keep header parsing as a shared library.

The table from architecture to chat format names model families, not models; it is acceptable, but should be treated as data.

items.name: Runtime fit logic (pure): Fit, largest_full_gpu_context, FIT_COMBINATIONS, fastest_combination, free_expert_blocks, default_micro_batch, calibrated_micro_batch_fits, load_without_mmap, weights_in_ram_bytes, micro_batch_args, probe_args, parse_fit_output, fitted_gpu_layers, tensor_overrides, spread, fit_combinations, FitDecision, fit_reuse
items.what_it_does: Pure decision rules. Finds the largest context that keeps every layer on the GPU, picks the fastest cache and margin, picks the batch size by the owner's speed rule, and decides whether to load weights into RAM and whether a remembered decision can be reused.
items.change: Keep as the pool manager's llama.cpp tuning library. Two additions: multiply the context by the number of slots for each copy, and include GPU memory already reserved for other copies on the same GPU.
items.evidence: pub async fn largest_full_gpu_context<F, Fut>(..probe_batch); pub fn fit_reuse(remembered, free_vram_mib, preferred)

items.name: probe, probe_in_order, FIT_PROBE_CONCURRENCY
items.what_it_does: Runs llama.cpp's fit tool as a child process, up to 4 at once, to ask how many layers of a model fit in GPU memory at a given context.
items.change: Run it on the machine and GPU that will host the copy (in Kubernetes, as a start-up step of the copy's pod, or as a job pinned to that node). Never run it on an API server.

items.name: fit_memory_key
items.what_it_does: Builds the key for a remembered fit from the model file's name, size and date, the fit tool's full path and date, the request, and total GPU memory.
items.change: Key it by model content hash, runtime build, GPU type and memory, and request, without local paths. Store it in PostgreSQL so every machine with the same GPU type reuses it.

items.name: parse_devices, gpu_startup_failure
items.what_it_does: Reads the runtime's device list, and recognises GPU start-up failures in its log (CUDA, Vulkan, HIP, SYCL errors) as opposed to bad files or port clashes.
items.change: Keep it unchanged in the pool manager.

items.name: cpu_configuration, without_load_tuning
items.what_it_does: Rewrites a load for CPU-only use: no GPU, f16 cache, context cap, and a RAM prompt cache sized from this machine's free RAM and the model file size. It adds a note advising smaller models.
items.change: Keep it for the CPU-only one-machine case. The free RAM must be that of the host running the copy, minus other copies. The advice note goes to the admin.

items.name: load_with_fallback
items.what_it_does: Tries to start the model on the GPU. If that fails, it tries the GPU again without the extra tuning, then silently falls back to CPU, and reports what happened.
items.change: Keep the retry steps. Whether a pool copy may fall back to CPU becomes an admin setting for each deployment; on a GPU server it is usually better to fail and alert. The result is recorded on the copy.

items.name: Calibration planning and choice (pure): Placement, Plan, thread_candidates, plan, micro_batch_candidates, micro_batch_plan, micro_batch_run_order, MicroBatchMeasurement, choose_micro_batch, measured_extra_blocks, Rate, Measurement, Profile, choose_profiles, Regression, regression, Environment, Calibration, model_key, parse_bench_json, bench_args, FittedPlacement, read_fitted_placement
items.what_it_does: Plans a speed benchmark of one model on one machine (thread counts, batch sizes). It turns the results into Fastest, Balanced and Light profiles, picks a batch size by the owner's speed rule, and flags slow-downs against an earlier comparable run.
items.change:
Keep as the library for the admin's calibration action.
- Results are stored for each GPU-machine type, not each laptop.
- 'Light' (leave cores free for other apps) matters only on a shared one-machine install.
- model_key (file name and size) becomes a content hash.

items.name: runtime_tool, run_tool, fitted_placement, run_benchmark, runtime_build
items.what_it_does: Runs the runtime's fit, benchmark and version tools as hidden child processes (with up to 30 minutes for a benchmark) and reads their output.

Changes needed:
- Downloads become an admin action queued as a worker job in PostgreSQL, with progress stored there.
- Files are written to the model store (S3, MinIO or a folder).
- The address is checked against the network policy (allowed hosts).

items.name: alerts_for, Alert
items.what_it_does: Warns about high GPU memory or RAM use and suggests reducing context, reducing GPU layers or stopping inference.
items.change: Alerts are raised for each machine and GPU on the admin dashboard, with suggestions aimed at admins (scale out, fewer copies on this GPU).

items.name: AppState fields models, inference, llama, downloads, load_progress, fit_preparation
items.what_it_does: In-memory shared state of the single program: model list with current model, stub engine, the one model server, download jobs, one load-progress record, and background fit-search flags.
items.change:
Remove these from the API server state.
- The registry, copies, downloads and progress move to PostgreSQL, owned by the pool manager and admin jobs.
- API servers keep only a gateway client and a short-lived read cache of the registry.

items.name: list_models (GET /api/models, /api/v1/models)
items.what_it_does: On every call it rescans the local models folder, updates the list, starts a background fit for new files, reads each model's tooling.json, and adds tool support from the SQLite record.
items.change: Return the models this user's groups allow. For each, include its ability profile and availability (ready copies, can wake up) from the database. Folder scanning becomes the admin import action, and the list call never touches disk.

items.name: load_model (POST /api/models/load)
items.what_it_does: Lets the user switch the one running model. It refuses if any chat or agent run is active, and reports progress in the single progress record.
items.change: Users no longer load models: choosing a model on a conversation is enough, and the gateway routes by model id. The admin gets 'deploy / set copies / scale' actions on the pool manager instead.

items.name: unload_models (POST /api/models/unload)
items.what_it_does: Stops the running model if no run is active, then restarts the background fit search.
items.change: Becomes the admin's 'scale model to zero' or 'stop copy' action. The pool manager drains that copy (no new requests, finish current ones) before stopping it.

items.name: inference_status (GET /api/inference/status)
items.what_it_does: Reports whether the one model server is running, its address, model, context, last error, and a CPU-mode notice.
items.change: Users get each allowed model's availability. The status of each copy, including its address, last error and CPU fallback, is admin-only.

items.name: inference_start (POST /api/inference/start)
items.what_it_does: Starts the model server for a model id, or for any file path and port the caller sends, falling back to the current model.
items.change: Admin-only 'start copy of registered model'. Remove the free file path and port from the request; ports are allocated by the pool manager. Audit every call.
items.evidence: InferenceStartReq { model_path: Option<String>, port: Option<u16>, .. }; (None, PathBuf::from(p)); req.port.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_SIDECAR_PORT)

items.name: tooling_for_load, tooling_identity
items.what_it_does: During a model load, uses the saved tool-check result or runs the check now (a few seconds), and tells the person loading what was found.
items.change: When a copy becomes ready and its model/runtime/template has no current profile, the pool manager queues a tool-check job. The load is never blocked, and the check runs once per model, not per copy. The notice goes to the admin.
items.evidence: set_progress(.., "checking_tools", ..); run_tool_check(s, model, base_url, cfg, runtime, template)

items.name: run_tool_check
items.what_it_does: Runs the tool check against a running model's address and saves the result beside the model file.
items.change: Worker job that calls the gateway with a model id (any copy, or the provider) and writes the ability profile to the database.

items.name: recheck_model_tooling (POST /api/models/:id/tooling/check)
items.what_it_does: Re-runs the tool check, but only if the requested model is the one loaded. It updates the running model's settings in memory.
items.change: Admin action that queues a check for any model id (self-hosted or provider). Gateways pick up the new profile from the database.

items.name: guard_agent_running
items.what_it_does: Blocks any model change while any chat reply or agent run is active anywhere in the program.
items.change: Replace it with per-copy draining. Taking a copy out of service stops new requests going to it and waits for its in-flight requests (and moves or pauses agent runs pinned to it). Other users and models are unaffected. Active runs are tracked in the database, not in one process.

items.name: fit_context_with_runtime, FitPurpose, batched_fit_holds, search_fit (and apply_fit_decision)
items.what_it_does: Asks llama.cpp's fit tool which context, cache and batch size keep the whole model on the GPU, checks that probes run together agree with probes run alone, and remembers the decision in the SQLite file.
items.change: Move it to the pool manager's start-copy path on the target machine. Store decisions in PostgreSQL keyed by GPU type. Count memory reserved by sibling copies, and only one copy starts on a GPU at a time, so two starts cannot both claim the same free memory.

items.name: FitPreparation, spawn_fit_preparation, prepare_fits, prepare_fit
items.what_it_does: A background job in this program that works out each model's fit ahead of its first load, but only while no model is running. It is cancelled the moment a load starts.
items.change: Run it per machine and GPU when a GPU is idle, or as the admin's 'prepare deployment' action, using the deployment's admin settings. If several models are always running it may never find an idle GPU, so the fit is mainly done at copy start.
items.evidence: if .. || s.llama.write().await.is_running() { return; }; models.sort_by_key(|model| model.id != settings.general.default_model)

items.name: start_sidecar
items.change: Becomes 'start one copy of model X on GPU G'. It never stops other copies. Settings come from the admin's deployment config. The result is a registry row, and the tool check is queued separately. Sampling settings are removed from the load (they become per request).
items.evidence: s.llama.write().await.stop().await; s.models.write().await.unload_all(); base_inference_config(&settings, ..); s.llama.write().await.running = Some(sidecar); s.models.write().await.switch_to(id)

items.name: inference_stop (POST /api/inference/stop)
items.what_it_does: Stops the running model when no run is active, and restarts the background fit search.
items.change: Admin 'stop copy or deployment' action with draining and an audit record.

items.name: scan_models (POST /api/models/scan)
items.what_it_does: Rescans the local models folder and updates the in-memory list.
items.change: Admin 'import models from store' action that runs a header-reading job and writes registry rows.

items.name: model_recommend (GET /api/models/:id/recommend)
items.what_it_does: Rule-of-thumb context recommendation using this machine's memory and the number of active agent runs.
items.change: Remove it. Fit decisions per GPU type, on the admin model page, replace it.

items.name: model_detail (GET /api/models/:id)
items.what_it_does: Shows a model's facts plus rough size and fit estimates, worked out from this machine and the user's context setting.
items.change: The admin view shows registry facts, fit decisions and calibrations per GPU type, and the copies. Users get a short model card: name, ability profile, context.

items.name: delete_model (DELETE /api/models/:id)
items.what_it_does: Permanently deletes a model's weights file from this disk, stopping the model first if it is the one loaded. It does not check for running work.
items.change: Admin-only, with an audit record. Drain and stop all copies of the model, remove its registry entry and permissions, then delete it from the model store.

items.name: Download handlers: list_downloads, start_download, get_download, pause_download, resume_download, cancel_download
items.what_it_does: Exposes the download manager: start a download from any address, list, get, pause, resume or cancel.
items.change: Admin-only endpoints over download jobs queued in PostgreSQL, checked against the network policy, writing to the model store.

items.name: load_model_by_id
items.what_it_does: Loads a registered model on the fixed port 3888, replacing whatever was running. It is used by the load button and the /model chat command.

items.name: prepare_conversation (POST /api/conversations/:id/prepare)

items.name: conversation_compatibility (GET compatibility for a pending switch)

items.name: benchmark (POST /api/system/benchmark)

surprises.title: Chat and agent requests never name a model: they use whatever is running
surprises.why_it_matters: A gateway with several models needs a model id on every request. Today a conversation's model_id is not used to answer it. The reply comes from the loaded model, and the conversation's 'last model' is overwritten with that model afterwards. A recovery screen exists only for this mismatch. Routing must resolve conversation model, then user's allowed list, then a copy, for chat, agent steps, compaction and summaries alike.
surprises.evidence: api.rs:3452-3463 sidecar = llama.running (base_url, cfg); agent_runner.rs:2619-2637 same snapshot; api.rs:4141-4149 set_last_model(cid, current()); api.rs:8767 stale filter c.last_model != loaded; api.rs:6840-6856 compaction uses the running sidecar

surprises.title: Each copy serves one conversation at a time; more slots split the context
surprises.why_it_matters: With --parallel 1, a second user's request queues behind the first and evicts its cached prompt. Raising the slot count makes llama.cpp divide --ctx-size across slots (unless a unified cache is used). The whole memory-fit search sizes the context for one slot, so the fit, the policy and the admin's concurrency setting must be designed together.
surprises.evidence: server_args: "--parallel".into(), "1".into(); fit_to_memory and largest_full_gpu_context size one context; prompt_cache_ram_mib sizes the RAM cache for switching conversations on one copy

surprises.title: Prompt-cache reuse depends on llama.cpp choosing the slot, and the side requests of a run must reach the same copy
surprises.evidence: sampling_body "cache_prompt": true; chat_turns_on_run_prompt doc: same request without tools 'matched none of the run's cached prompt ... read in full (35,087 and 33,734 tokens)'; api.rs:126-135 legacy_prompt_order keeps prefix byte-identical

surprises.title: An agent run captures one server address at start and fails if that process dies
surprises.why_it_matters: On a worker, a copy can be scaled in or restarted mid-run. Today the run never moves: it checks the in-process manager and stops with 'model server stopped'. The worker needs gateway health from the pool registry and re-routing to another copy (or pausing, as is decided for app disconnects).
surprises.evidence: agent_runner.rs:2619-2637 snapshot (base_url, cfg); 3020-3029 stopped between steps => S::Failed; 3126 retry only while llama.is_running(); 3201-3211

surprises.title: Starting a copy can kill sibling copies on Windows
surprises.why_it_matters: Before each start, every model-server process running the same program file whose parent process is gone is killed. With several copies on one Windows machine, a restart of the pool manager makes every surviving copy an 'orphan', and the next start kills them all. Reclaiming must be limited to copies the manager recorded.
surprises.evidence: reap_orphaned_sidecars: filter exe()==target && parent missing => process.kill(); called in RunningSidecar::spawn before binding

surprises.title: Memory fit and calibration assume they have the whole GPU
surprises.evidence: api.rs:1680/1702 prepare_fits returns if llama.is_running(); api.rs:9809-9812 calibrate stops model; metrics.rs:82-87 busiest card; hardware.rs:105-114 GPUs 'not enumerated'; server_args emits only --device none

surprises.title: Sampling values for every request are fixed into the model's load settings from one user's settings
surprises.why_it_matters: Temperature, top-p, top-k and repeat penalty are copied from the single settings object when the model is loaded. Every later request reuses them, so the company, group and user setting levels cannot apply per user without separating sampling from the launch configuration.
surprises.evidence: base_inference_config: temperature: settings.inference.temperature, top_p, top_k, repeat_penalty; sampling_body uses cfg.temperature etc.

surprises.title: The engine interface the comments describe does not exist; a fake engine is kept as a status mirror
surprises.why_it_matters: The model gateway must be built new from the HTTP client code; there is no working abstraction to extend. Several status endpoints read context and speed from the stub (fake) engine instead of real data, so they must be rewritten rather than moved.
surprises.evidence: inference.rs:3 'The rest of the application talks to IInferenceEngine'; LlamaCppEngine.generate returns 'not wired yet'; api.rs:2079-2085 'Mirror loaded state into the registry + stub engine for UI consistency'; system_info/cache_budget read s.inference

surprises.title: Tool input formats are hard-coded for built-in tools only
surprises.why_it_matters: Plugin and MCP tools offered natively to a model would get an empty input format, and the forced answer format lists only the built-in registry. The ability profile and the plugin description files must supply each tool's format, or native tool calling will not work for plugins.
surprises.evidence: tooling.rs parameters(): match on "list_directory", ..., _ => (json!({}), &[]); llamaserver.rs:1623 for tool in crate::tools::registry()

surprises.title: Request bodies include fields standard OpenAI and Anthropic APIs do not accept
surprises.why_it_matters:
Several fields in every request are llama.cpp extensions:
- cache_prompt, top_k, repeat_penalty, timings_per_token, chat_template_kwargs;
- a response_format of type json_object with a schema.
The hosted OpenAI API refuses unknown request fields (from general knowledge of that API, not checked here), and the Anthropic API uses a different format. The adapter split is a requirement before any outside provider works, not polish. Reporting the outside model's speed also needs a replacement for the llama.cpp timings data.
surprises.evidence: sampling_body json; apply_options chat_template_kwargs; structured_action_schema {"type":"json_object","schema":..}; stream(): body["timings_per_token"]=true

surprises.title: Any caller can start a model from any file path, and download from any address
surprises.why_it_matters: The start endpoint takes a free file path and port from the request body, and the download endpoint accepts any http(s) address and writes to the server's disk. In a multi-user service both must be admin-only, audited, and checked against the network policy (downloads could otherwise reach internal addresses).
surprises.evidence: InferenceStartReq { model_path, port }; (None, PathBuf::from(p)); DownloadManager::validate_request only checks the https:// / http:// prefix

surprises.title: Cancelling a load stops the running model for everyone
surprises.why_it_matters: cancel_load stops the model server without the active-work check. With many users, one user's cancel would end every other user's replies and runs. Cancel must apply only to a starting copy and must be admin-only.

surprises.title: The system overview lists every conversation without owner scoping
surprises.why_it_matters: system_overview returns the 20 latest conversation titles from the whole database. In a multi-user service that leaks other users' titles. It must become an admin aggregate without conversation titles, or be scoped to the owner.
surprises.evidence: let convs = st.list_conversations(); convs.into_iter().take(20).map(|c| json!({"id": c.id, "title": c.title, ..}))

surprises.title: Model identity is file name plus size, and fit keys contain local paths
surprises.why_it_matters: Calibrations, template capabilities and tool checks are keyed by 'name:size'. Fit decisions also include the fit tool's absolute path and the file's modification date. Across machines and a shared model store these keys either collide (same name and size) or never match (different paths). A content hash and a machine-type key are needed.
surprises.evidence: calibration::model_key = format!("{name}:{size}"); fit_memory_key includes fit_tool.display() and modified(model); storage.rs:1232 template_caps keyed by model_key

surprises.title: Load settings live in the single user settings object, and changing them refits
surprises.why_it_matters: The design says performance, tuning and model management belong to the admin. Today context size, automatic tuning, hardware threads and GPU layers, cache precision, drafting and the calibration profile are user settings. They are validated in put_settings, and a change restarts the fit search. They must move to admin settings for each deployment, and the user settings form must lose them, or users will tune shared GPUs.
surprises.evidence: put_settings validates next.inference.context_size, next.hardware.*, next.runtime.kv_cache, next.runtime.speculative; previous.runtime != next.runtime => spawn_fit_preparation

surprises.title: The tool check runs inside the load and blocks it
surprises.why_it_matters: start_sidecar runs the tool check before it marks the model ready, so the first load of a new model waits several seconds for 2 to 4 probe requests. With copies scaled automatically, the check must run once per (model, runtime, template) as a separate job, never per copy and never on the start path.
surprises.evidence: start_sidecar: tooling_for_load(s, model, &binary, &base_url, &sidecar.cfg).await before s.llama.write().await.running = Some(sidecar)
